providerQuiescenceContract20261023.scope: Targeted actual per-actor reservation/worker/cleanup trace in both installed provider variants; original files unchanged.
observedContract: AR_Rappel_From_Heli reserves a server-local AR_Rappelling_Player_index slot and publishes actor AR_Is_Rappelling before starting the actor-owner worker. It returns no structured acceptance/completion receipt.
The server slot-retirement worker polls actor flag/death every2s, without an original task deadline. Actor flag clear does not prove the server slot has retired.
Actor worker destroys ropes/devices, clears public AR_Is_Rappelling and AR_Rappelling_Vehicle, then sleeps2s and unconditionally calls allowDamage true. The bundle variant has the same ordering.

Earlier landing/fall branches also write allowDamage true. A current true damage readback or elapsed2s after flag clear cannot prove the final scheduled worker has executed; scheduler delay and indistinguishable intervening script writes remain.
The bulk API additionally runs its own unbounded helicopter/group controller. Using it would evade CBE flight ownership and finite-operation requirements.
providerQuiescenceContract20261023.impact: Current read-only runtime-marker compatibility yields during active rope state only; it is not a complete provider-cleanup acknowledgement. No CBE rappel executor is present. Do not advertise a working insertion module or infer completed handback from flag false.
providerQuiescenceContract20261023.requiredImplementation: Retain the requested finite cargo insertion feature. Implement controlled rope execution with explicit actual-owner acceptance, original task deadline, exact mission damage baseline, completion after all cleanup, and no stale delayed writes; or use a provider API revision that supplies those guarantees. Mere dependency detection, arbitrary grace time or a wrapper around the current bulk API is insufficient. Preserve group identity, actual stable flight and ground/roof arrival requirements.

workerHandleTrace20261024.question: Can a CBE wrapper observe scriptDone on existing provider workers instead of inferring completion from early activity flags?
workerHandleTrace20261024.finding: No complete task graph is exposed. Server actor API spawns the movement worker without saving/publishing its handle, then spawns a distinct slot-retirement worker. A last spawned value, if captured from that server call, identifies slot bookkeeping, not the actor task graph. Nonserver dispatch returns remote-wrapper transport semantics, not an actor-worker SCRIPT handle. No provider code executed to infer undocumented return types.

workers.name: actor owner movement
workers.effect: Owns movement, physics, ropes/devices and delayed unconditional damage write after public activity clears. Handle unretained by public API.

workers.name: server slot retirement

workers.name: actor animation

workers.name: remote animation replicas

workers.name: overspeed detach observer

workers.name: sound loops
workers.effect: Separate presentation workers; not treated as proof of physical control or terminal cleanup.

workerHandleTrace20261024.implementationDecision: Do not implement public-API wrapper success from one script handle, remoteExec return, all visible flags false or arbitrary grace. Existing provider marker detection remains incomplete compatibility, not insertion execution.

primitiveFindings: Point discovery itself issues no actor movement, but scans complete AP_RAPPEL_POINTS/custom mapping lists and all declared points without a hard input cap. Dynamic fallback uses6 hull queries each allowing100 hits; it is sparse model geometry, not safe rope routing/landing proof. Do not call it blindly as a bounded CBE primitive.

Actor movement uses a hidden can anchor and hidden AA device, two native ropes, per-iteration gravity/wind/rope-length integration and actor transforms. Source entry force-exits and randomly shifts the actor; source device overshoots its computed position by factor6. Landing can snap up to5m onto a probed surface. These are redesign points, not accepted CBE recovery or arrival evidence.

Actor worker starts separate delayed AI-descent, overspeed and animation writers. Animation replication starts additional delayed switchMove/switchGesture loops; AnimChanged can force another pose. Cleanup unconditionally enables simulation; actor cleanup restores damage true after activity is already cleared. Capturing only the main actor script handle still cannot acknowledge this graph.

Pure point/weapon/patch reads can inform an adapted task, but native provider actor/bulk/animation APIs cannot be used unchanged as CBE-owned finite execution. Source animation assets can remain dependency-provided; visual/body/grip quality requires actual in-engine review.
